svg.text: Three-node Raft HA: drop database via a replica propagates removal to every peer

g.text: 3 ArcadeDB containers on one Docker network, all given the same Raft server list.
All containers start in parallel; Testcontainers waits for each node's HTTP health probe.
Every node's cluster endpoint is polled once a second until one of them claims leadership.
GET /api/v1/cluster -> body contains "isLeader":true (the run fails after 60s)
Database and schema are written through the leader, which Raft carries to every follower.
CREATE VERTEX TYPE User, Photo - EDGE TYPE HasUploaded, FriendOf, Likes - UNIQUE_HASH / FULL_TEXT / GEOSPATIAL
A fixture of 30 users and 300 photos is written and must reach every node before the drop.
Every RemoteDatabase is closed before the drop: no open connection may point at a database about to vanish.
db0.close(); db1.close(); db2.close(); (also closed in the catch block, so a failure cannot leak them)
The drop is issued on a replica on purpose - that is the forward-to-leader path this test exists to cover.
The removal is confirmed from the outside: the database must disappear from every node's database list.
Dropping the same database again has to fail: idempotent success would hide a drop that never happened.
assertThat(secondDropStatus).isBetween(400, 499) - tearDown skips compareAllDatabases, the DB is gone on purpose
